stem: double cropping in agriculture means raising of

options.label: c
options.text: One crop along with another crop

expl: In agriculture, double cropping means growing crops one after another on the same land within one year, that is, growing two crops in different seasons. For example, under this system, a spring barley crop, winter wheat crop, or potato crop is grown before the main crops such as rice and maize, thus producing two successive crops. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

stem: Which one of the following most appropriately describes the nature of the Green Revolution of the late sixties of 20th century?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Green Revolution in India is considered to have started in the 1960s, when high-yielding seeds began to be used. Along with this, greater use of fertilizers and strong emphasis on the development of irrigation facilities were also made.

stem: Who is credited with the Green Revolution in India?

expl: The Green Revolution began in India in the 1960s. Dr. M. S. Swaminathan is known as the father of the Green Revolution in India.

stem:
What is true about the second Green Revolution in India?
1. It aims at further increasing the production of wheat and rice in areas already benefited from the Green Revolution.
2. It aims at extending seed-water-fertilizer technology to areas which could not benefit from Green Revolution.
3. It aims at increasing yields of crops other than those used for the Green Revolution in the beginning.
4. It aims at integrating cropping with animal husbandry, social forestry and fishing
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
expl: The objective of the Second Green Revolution in India is to expand seeds, water, fertilizers, and technology to those areas which have not been able to benefit from the Green Revolution so far, and to integrate crop production with animal husbandry, social forestry, and fisheries. In the Second Green Revolution, it has not been stated that the crops used during the First Green Revolution should be left out.

stem:
Select the component of the Green Revolution by using the given code :
1. High-yielding varieties of seeds
2. Irrigation
3. Rural Electrification
4. Rural roads and marketing
Code :
expl: In India, in the 1960s, promoting high-yielding variety seeds, fertilizers, irrigation, and other technical practices came to be known as the Green Revolution. Therefore, in the context of the Green Revolution, option (a) is the correct answer.

stem: The success of the Green Revolution depends on the availability of—
expl: The Green Revolution was started in the 1960s as a package programme, which included the following inputs— (i) high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, (ii) fertilizers, (iii) pesticides, and (iv) adequate irrigation facilities, etc. Although all the above four factors are necessary for the Green Revolution, the high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds played a crucial role in bringing the Green Revolution.

On 28 July, 2000, the Central Government announced the new National Agricultural Policy. Under this new policy, the concept of the Rainbow Revolution was presented. Under it, directly or indirectly, all revolutions related to the agricultural sector were included; for example—Green Revolution, White Revolution, Yellow Revolution, Blue Revolution, Red Revolution, Golden Revolution, Brown Revolution, and Silver Revolution.

stem: Which of the following crops saw the highest increase in production due to the Green Revolution?
expl: In India, due to the Green Revolution, the highest rate of increase was seen in wheat production. The Green Revolution began in the 1960s in Indian agriculture with high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds. In India, M. S. Swaminathan is considered the father of the Green Revolution.
